review_text_raw:
Before I leave my review of this game, I want to say that this game is vaguely similar to 'Orwell' but this branches off into a better sub-genre. The emphasis is more about the storyline and puzzles with a slightly worse UI. For reference I hated Orwell and found it to be a chore to finish but loved this. Bear in mind that this game's storyline is quite dark and although isn't incredibly graphic might cause discomfort to some.

Firstly I should note that this is from a developer from Hong Kong, so there are a few minor translation issues that remain in the game. It's about 99.9% translated but has 1 or 2 notable translations that aren't translated properly which impacts your ability to solve a clue. I had to google both of these as they made no sense and stalled me completely.

Another concern is that the game absolutely does not let you press the Escape key on your keyboard which means that chapter introduction cinematics aren't skippable and it leads to 1-2 occasions where you have to ALT+F4 because you are on a screen that you cannot escape from. Without giving spoilers, if you attempt to phone hack in chapter 2 without having the number saved you will be hard-locked on a screen asking for the phone number you don't have.

Other notable bugs include not being able to 100% chapter 3 due to a typo (which I have reported) in a name. You can complete the mission absolutely fine but you won't be able to get the steam achievement for perfecting it.

Aside from the slower pacing in the first Chapter, which is essentially a tutorial mission that you are getting in the demo, the game feels incredibly smooth. Chapters 2-4 escalate in story line with a surprisingly good plot that caught me out as these games generally have an astoundingly basic storyline. Chapter 5 was an absolute roller coaster of detective work and difficulty and really gave the game a good way to end the current allotment of the game. The plot concluded quite well but left a cliffhanger for the next instalments which tie in nicely.

The timed elements feel off in some places, I genuinely have no idea how you are supposed to solve puzzles in the time they give you and complete the sequence in full with time to finish. For most users there needs to be additional clues before you enter the timed event or possibly an extra minute or two to compensate. Although the last mission is incredibly hectic I feel that's the one place the timer is very apt for the staple endings. The "perfect ending" does require some degree of grind but it's well placed and gives an satisfying albeit frustrating end. I think it took me ~1hr to solve it and a further 10mins to execute it perfectly.

Really can't wait for any additional chapters for DLC they release. £8 for this game is very reasonable, as the re-play value outside of achievement hunting isn't really there. It's an incredibly linear game with an open ending which you can save/load to see the other outcomes.

review_text_raw:
Honestly for an EA game, this has potential.
-Well acted voice overs where appropriate
-Excellent little mini-games and timed sections which break up the regular pacing of the game for a small hint of excitement
-Comfortable UI and UX aspects.

However, that does not mean that the game is free of bugs, nor does not need some shine and polishing in other areas.
-The localisation for English needs a lot of work. I understand and appreciate that English may not be the primary language of the devs, it can be jarring and de-imsersifying (probably just created a word there) in places where the flow and writing gets jumbled, lacks conveyance and flow. -If- English is going to be the primary release language, then additional work needs to be done polishing that up, as reading through news stories, toothbook posts and hitalk app conversations are so critical to gameplay in Cyber Manhunter. 

- While the gameplay is interesting, and slowly reveals itself over time, save for a few set pieces (phone trojans, the chapter 3 end setpiece, and phone conversations) the gameplay is very samey: 
      - Get information on Person A
      - Crack Person A's stuff using the database to get incomplete information Person B 
      - Rinse and repeat for B to C and so on. 
Don't get me wrong this is a fine mechanic core mechanic but in the second and third chapters (which are where the breaks from core mechanics really should be kicking in) there's not enough divergence from that key mechanic which in my opinion mutes the game just a little bit. 

- Finally: Replayability at this point is low. 4 hours in and with enough snooping and combing through what is a series of engrossing stories, I can truthfully say there's nothing to come back to for now. Certainly if you just focused on drilling down exactly what you needed for the main objective of each chapter you would find that yeah, coming back to perfect a chapter would be worthwhile, but then after that you're pretty much done. 
I'm not sure if its on the horizon or not, but something that could randomise a mission, or a free play or something that would beef-up the very nicely put together experience that is Cyber Manhunter and keep me playing it longer would be appreciated, as I thoroughly enjoyed my Friday night with it. 

I know it looks like I've gone into more detail with the current drawbacks than I have the pros of the game, however what Cyber Manhunter does right it does beautifully. This review is more....feedback than anything else, and hopefully something the devs see. For you the player, this is definitely something you can pick up, play and get hooked into. A good Friday night relaxing beer and investigate game that makes you think. Well worth the price of admission at this point and I look forward to what is provided by the developers moving forward.

review_text_raw:
Cyber Manhunt plunges players into the gritty and morally ambiguous world of cyber investigation. As an investigator, you use hacking, social engineering, and deduction skills to uncover hidden truths behind various cases. The game's strengths lie in its immersive narrative and realistic depiction of the internet's darker corners.

Pros:

Compelling Storyline: Each case is engaging, with twists that keep you hooked.
Realistic Mechanics: The hacking and investigative processes feel authentic, enhancing immersion.
Ethical Dilemmas: The game forces you to confront tough moral choices, adding depth to the gameplay.

Cons:

Steep Learning Curve: The mechanics can be challenging for newcomers, potentially leading to frustration.
Pacing Issues: Some parts of the game feel slow, which can disrupt the overall flow. 
Making a mistake while in a dialogue section requires you to sit through it all again because you can't skip dialogue. 

Overall, Cyber Manhunt offers a fun experience for fans of investigative and narrative-driven games.
